Crossfitting example

Introduction

Simple crossfitting example

library(caret)
library(sjPlot)

Any parameters go here:

  • k: number of folds
  • n_samples: number of samples
set.seed(42)
k_folds = 5
n_samples = 10000

One confounder, one treatment

Data

x1 = rnorm(n_samples, mean = 0, sd = 1)

x1_t = 2

t = x1 * x1_t + rnorm(n_samples, 0, 0.5)

plot(x1, t)
x1_y = 1.5
t_y = 2.5

y = x1 * x1_y + t * t_y + rnorm(n_samples, 0, 0.25)

plot(x1, y)
plot(t, y)
df = data.frame(x1, t, y)

Classic causal model

mod_lm = lm(y ~ t + x1, df)
tab_model(mod_lm)
  y
Predictors Estimates CI p
(Intercept) 0.00 -0.00 – 0.01 0.424
t 2.51 2.50 – 2.52 <0.001

R2 / R2 adjusted 0.999 / 0.999

FWL method with cross-fitting

folds <- createFolds(df$y, k = k_folds)

df$t_hat = df$y_hat = NA

for (k in 1:k_folds) {
  ## Split data
  df_train = df[-folds[[k]], ]
  df_test = df[folds[[k]], ]

  ## Propensity model
  mod = lm(t ~ x1, df_train)
  df$t_hat[folds[[k]]] = predict(mod, newdata = df_test)
  
  ## Outcome model
  mod = lm(y ~ x1, df_train)
  df$y_hat[folds[[k]]] = predict(mod, newdata = df_test)

}

df$t_res = df$t - df$t_hat
df$y_res = df$y - df$y_hat
## Final model
mod_final = lm(y_res ~ t_res - 1, df) ## Remove intercept
tab_model(mod_final)
  y_res
Predictors Estimates CI p
t res 2.51 2.50 – 2.51 <0.001
Observations 10000
R2 / R2 adjusted 0.961 / 0.961
